texts.preamble: Smt.Lakshmi Devi P vs Tata Aig General Insurance on 26 April, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This day of 26th day of April 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.4521/2018 Petitioner Smt.Lakshmi Devi P., Aged about 35 years, Wife of Mahesh Kumar G., No.824, Gollara Palya, Bengaluru-560 091. (By Pleader Shri Puttswamy H.) V/s. Respondents 1. Tata Aig General Insurance Company Limited, Race Course Road Left to No.59, 3rd floor, Jp & Dj Arpad, Millers Road, Bengaluru-560 054. Policy No.0182826138/0000000/00 valid from 17.8.2017 to 16.8.2018 2 Scch-18 Mvc 4521/2018 (By Pleader Shri K.Sridhara) 2. Laxshminarasimhaiah G.P., Son of Puttanarasimaiah, Channamariahana Palya, Tavarekere Hobli, Thippagondanahalli, Bengaluru South-562 130. (Exparte) Smt.Lakshmi Devi P vs Tata Aig General Insurance on 26 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117312971/ 1 J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.12,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 10.4.2018 at about 1.30 p.m., the petitioner was a pillion rider on a motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 proceeding on Hosahalli road, Doddagollarahatti, Bengaluru at that time, the rider of the said motor cycle rode the same with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and suddenly applied the break and jumped the path holes. As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries. Immediately she was shifted to Shri Krishna hospital, Gollarahatti, Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident she was hale and healthy, aged about 35 years, doing tailoring work and earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549. Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has appeared before the court and filed its written statements. The respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court, placed exparte. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 are as under: The respondent No.1 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 and its validity. Further denied the manner of the accident, involvement of the vehicle. Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against it with cost. 6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed: 7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner herself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P12. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.1 has not examined any witness on its behalf.
texts.arguments: Further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant. During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved her case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent has argued that the offending vehicle bearing No.KA-02-JK-4549 has not at all involved in the accident and prays to dismiss the petition as against the respondents. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). The contention of the petitioner is that, she has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses. 24. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 35 years. Due to severe injuries she is permanently disabled. The petitioner has not examined the doctor to speak about the grievousness of the injuries or to assess the disability. Therefore no amount is granted under this head. 25. Further contention of the petitioner is that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
